content.value_statement: WordPress Abilities API work requires careful hooks, REST metadata, and permission checks. This skill guides PHP registration, REST exposure, and JavaScript consumption.
actual_capabilities: Guides registration of ability categories before abilities using documented hooks.
Lists required metadata such as label, description, category, readonly, and show_in_rest.
Helps debug missing REST exposure under wp-abilities/v1 endpoints.
Recommends @wordpress/abilities for client-side access and checks.
Points to reference guides for PHP registration and REST API checks.
Highlights permission_callback and schemas for safer abilities.
limitations: Targets WordPress 6.9+ and may need a plugin or package for earlier versions.
Requires a WordPress project context and does not create a full plugin by itself.
Some verification steps require a running WordPress environment and WP-CLI.
Provides guidance and does not replace official WordPress documentation.

use_cases.title: Register a plugin ability
use_cases.description: Add a namespaced ability with labels, schemas, metadata, and permissions in a plugin or mu-plugin.

use_cases.title: Expose abilities through REST
use_cases.description: Confirm show_in_rest, endpoint names, and category registration when clients cannot find an ability.

use_cases.title: Wire client-side checks
use_cases.description: Use @wordpress/abilities patterns to read available abilities and gate interface behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Find existing usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery in an unfamiliar WordPress repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: In this WordPress repo, find existing Abilities API usage and summarize where categories, abilities, and REST exposure are defined.

prompt_templates.title: Register a read-only ability
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic implementation for an informational ability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a read-only WordPress Abilities API ability for [purpose]. Use the correct hooks, a namespaced ID, show_in_rest, and tests if available.

prompt_templates.title: Debug missing REST exposure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate troubleshooting when a client cannot find an ability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose why ability [ability-id] is missing from wp-abilities/v1. Check registration order, meta.show_in_rest, category IDs, and REST routes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a full integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced feature design across PHP, REST, and JavaScript.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Abilities API integration for [feature]. Include PHP registration, input and output schemas, permission_callback logic, REST verification, and @wordpress/abilities usage.

output_examples.input: Register a read-only site information ability.
output_examples.output: A plan that registers a category first, adds a namespaced ability, marks it read-only, exposes it to REST, and recommends permission checks.

output_examples.input: A client cannot see an ability in REST.
output_examples.output: A debugging checklist covering route availability, show_in_rest metadata, category mismatch, hook timing, and cache effects.

output_examples.input: Add JavaScript consumption for an ability.
output_examples.output: Guidance for adding @wordpress/abilities to the build, reading available abilities, and gating UI behavior based on capability checks.

best_practices: Register categories before abilities using the Abilities API hooks.
Use stable namespaced IDs, input schemas, output schemas, and permission callbacks.
Verify REST exposure and client behavior in a real WordPress environment.
anti_patterns: Exposing mutating abilities without a permission_callback.
Assuming REST exposure works without meta.show_in_rest and endpoint checks.

faq.question: What WordPress version does this target?
faq.answer: It targets WordPress 6.9+. Earlier projects may need the Abilities API plugin or package.

faq.question: Can it help with PHP registration?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides category registration, ability registration, metadata, schemas, and permissions.

faq.question: Can it debug missing abilities?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks hook timing, category IDs, show_in_rest, REST routes, and client query paths.

faq.question: Does it cover JavaScript clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends @wordpress/abilities for client-side access and interface checks.

faq.question: Does it replace official docs?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes common workflows and points to canonical WordPress references when needed.

faq.question: Does it require WP-CLI?
faq.answer: Not always. Some verification and environment checks may require WP-CLI or a running WordPress site.
